1. **Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA)** is calculated at the end of each semester as:
   \[ \text{SGPA} = \frac{\sum (C_i \times G_i)}{\sum C_i} \]
   where \(C_i\) denotes the credit weight of the \(i\)-th course and \(G_i\) is the numerical grade point secured.
2. **Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA)** is the weighted cumulative measure across all completed semesters:
   \[ \text{CGPA} = \frac{\sum_{\text{all}} (C_k \times G_k)}{\sum_{\text{all}} C_k} \]

RESIDENCE
1.1 Objective and Residential Community Standards
The residential halls at Apex Institute of Technology & Higher Sciences are envisioned as vibrant learning communities
promoting scholarship, camaraderie, civic responsibility, and mutual respect. Living on campus is a privilege extended to
enrolled students subject to strict adherence to institutional standards and codes of conduct.
1.2 Room Allocation and Possession Protocols
1. Rooms in residential halls are allocated annually by the Chief Warden’s Office based on seniority, academic standing
(CGPA), and program requirements.
2. First-year and second-year undergraduate students are mandated to reside in shared double-occupancy rooms in
Junior Residential Quads (Blocks A through D).
3. Single-occupancy rooms in Senior Towers (Blocks E, F, and G) are reserved exclusively for third-year, fourth-year, and
postgraduate students maintaining a minimum CGPA of 7.50 without active disciplinary reprimands.
4. Room allotment is non-transferable. Subletting, unauthorized swapping of rooms, or sheltering unregistered individuals
is an offense resulting in immediate cancellation of hostel allotment and forfeiture of the caution deposit.
5. Inmates must complete a physical inventory check-sheet at the time of taking possession, cataloging the condition of
furniture, electrical fittings, window screens, and study carrels.

chunks.section: CHAPTER 2: RESIDENTIAL CODE OF CONDUCT & COMMUNITY DISCIPLINE
chunks.text:
2.1 General Decorum and Civility
All residents must treat fellow residents, administrative wardens, security personnel, mess workers, and maintenance
staff with dignity and respect. Verbal abuse, harassment, intimidation, or disruptive behavior will attract severe disciplinary
action under the Standing Student Disciplinary Ordinance.
2.2 Anti-Ragging Statutory Declaration
1. Ragging in any shape, manner, or form—whether physical, psychological, verbal, electronic, or communicative—is
strictly prohibited by Supreme Court mandates and Institute regulations.
2. Any resident found engaging in, abetting, or failing to report incidents of ragging shall face immediate suspension,
summary eviction from the hostel, filing of a First Information Report (FIR) with the state police authorities, and permanent
expulsion from the Institute.
2.3 Prohibited Substances and Contraband
1. The entire residential campus is an absolute Zero-Tolerance Zone for alcoholic beverages, tobacco products, vaping
devices, narcotics, psychotropic substances, and flammable fireworks.
2. Possession, consumption, or storage of liquor, illicit drugs, or drug paraphernalia inside hostel rooms or residential
common areas shall lead to immediate expulsion and criminal prosecution.
2.4 Electrical Safety and Prohibited Appliances
1. To prevent electrical overloads and fire hazards, students are strictly prohibited from using high-wattage electrical
heating appliances inside hostel rooms. This includes electric immersion heaters, hotplates, induction cooktops, room
heaters, electric kettles exceeding 500W, and toaster ovens.
2. Permitted electrical devices are limited to laptop chargers, mobile phone chargers, table lamps, and personal hair
dryers (under 1000W).
3. Unauthorized appliances will be confiscated on discovery, and an administrative fine of Rs. 3,000 shall be levied per
confiscated item.

chunks.section: CHAPTER 3: CAMPUS INGRESS, EGRESS, AND NIGHT CURFEW REGULATIONS
chunks.text:
3.1 Mandatory Campus Ingress & Night Curfew [STRICT RESIDENTIAL LOCKDOWN POLICY]
All campus entrance gates, library halls, and academic departmental complexes shall be locked strictly at 22:00 hours
(10:00 PM). All resident students must be physically inside their assigned hostel blocks by 22:00 hours. No student is
permitted outside their hostel block under any circumstance between 22:00 hours and 06:00 hours. Security supervisors
at hostel entrances are mandated to log biometric attendance and physically bolt the external iron security gates promptly
at 22:00 hours. Any resident student arriving at the hostel gate after 22:00 hours shall have their name entered into the
Late Entry Violation Register, incur an automatic fine of Rs. 1,000 for the first offense, and be referred to the Chief
Warden. There are absolutely no exceptions to this curfew, regardless of departmental projects, study groups, or
extracurricular activities.
3.2 Night Outstation Pass Protocol
1. Any resident requiring to travel out of town or stay overnight away from the campus must submit a formal Night
Outstation Pass via the Student ERP Portal at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance.
2. The Outstation Pass must be authenticated by written parental consent dispatched from the registered parental
telephone number or email address on file.
3. Returning students must punch their biometric clearance at the main gate and deposit their signed slip with the resident
block warden.
3.3 Emergency Medical Exemption
In instances of acute medical distress occurring during curfew hours (22:00 to 06:00), the resident on-duty warden must
be immediately contacted. The warden will arrange for the campus emergency ambulance to convey the patient to the
University Medical Center. Under no circumstances should individual students venture unaccompanied past the hostel
gates during curfew.

operating hotplates in rooms will be penalized under Chapter 2.4.

rooms is deemed theft and will incur a community service penalty.

chunks.section: CHAPTER 6: MAINTENANCE, DAMAGE LIABILITY, AND CAUTION DEPOSITS
chunks.text:
6.1 Routine Room Maintenance
1. Housekeeping personnel clean common areas, corridors, washrooms, and stairwells daily between 08:30 hours and
14:00 hours.
2. Cleaning of private dorm rooms is the personal responsibility of the individual residents. Rooms must be kept hygienic,
orderly, and free of waste accumulations.
3. Maintenance requests for plumbing, carpentry, or electrical repairs must be submitted electronically through the
Campus Facilities Helpdesk ticket system.
6.2 Property Damage and Group Liability
1. If institutional furniture, fixtures, ceiling fans, glass windowpanes, or electronic infrastructure in a hostel room suffer
damage due to negligence or malice, the repairing cost plus a 25% administrative levy will be deducted from the
occupants' Hostel Caution Deposit.
2. In cases where property damage occurs in shared common areas (such as television lounges, elevators, water cooler
stations, or corridors) and the specific perpetrator cannot be identified, collective group liability shall be levied equally
across all residents of that floor or residential wing.

chunks.section: CHAPTER 8: WARDEN ADVISORY COMMITTEE & DISCIPLINARY SANCTIONS
chunks.text:
8.1 Disciplinary Sanction Scale
Infractions of this handbook shall be adjudicated by the Hostel Disciplinary Committee (HDC), presided over by the Chief
Warden. Sanctions range in severity:
- Level 1 (Minor Violation): Written warning notice and mandatory parent notification.
- Level 2 (Moderate Violation): Administrative monetary fine ranging from Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000, along with mandatory
community service (e.g., library catalog assistance).
- Level 3 (Severe Violation): Suspension of hostel residency for one semester, forfeiture of hostel fees, and formal
notation on the student's conduct certificate.
- Level 4 (Critical / Criminal Breach): Permanent expulsion from all campus housing, academic suspension, and referral
to law enforcement.
8.2 Appeals Procedure
A student penalized by the HDC may lodge a formal appeal to the Dean of Student Affairs within five (5) business days of
the sanction notice. The decision of the Dean of Student Affairs shall be final and binding.

chunks.section: CHAPTER 9: HOSTEL SUSTAINABILITY, RECYCLING & WATER CONSERVATION
chunks.text:
9.1 Environmental Responsibility & Conservation Protocols
Apex Institute of Technology is committed to maintaining a net-zero, environmentally sustainable residential campus.
Residents are required to actively participate in energy and water conservation initiatives:
1. All residents must switch off lights, ceiling fans, computer monitors, and exhaust fans whenever exiting dorm rooms or
common study chambers. Defaulting rooms identified during random security sweeps will be subject to a collective green
audit levy of Rs. 500 per incident.
2. Water waste through dripping taps or leaking cisterns must be reported within two hours to the plumbing helpdesk. The
washing of personal vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles within residential courtyards using hostel hosepipes is strictly
forbidden.
3. Waste segregation at source is mandatory. Residents must utilize designated color-coded collection bins: Green for
organic food waste, Blue for dry paper and cardboard, and Red for electronic waste or broken metal parts.
9.2 Solar Water Heating Infrastructure
Hostel blocks are equipped with centralized rooftop solar water heating collectors. Solar hot water supply is scheduled
daily from 06:00 hours to 09:30 hours and 18:00 hours to 20:30 hours during winter months. Tampering with roof
plumbing valves or safety relief fixtures constitutes severe physical vandalism under Chapter 6.

chunks.section: CHAPTER 10: RESIDENT WELFARE COUNCIL & GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL
chunks.text:
10.1 Composition of the Residential Hall Council
Each residential hostel block maintains an elected Student Welfare Council comprising:
- Block General Secretary (senior resident)
- Dining & Mess Committee Convener
- Sports & Cultural Representative
- Health, Sanitation, and Green Audit Secretary
The Council meets bi-weekly with the Resident Warden to evaluate mess meal quality, review facilities maintenance
tickets, coordinate intra-hostel tournaments, and propose community improvements.
10.2 Formal Complaint Filing and Escalation Timeline
1. Routine maintenance complaints must be resolved within forty-eight (48) hours of electronic ticket logging.
2. In the event of unresolved grievances, residents may escalate issues sequentially: First to the Resident Warden, then
to the Chief Warden, and ultimately to the Dean of Student Affairs.
3. Anonymous, frivolous, or retaliatory complaints directed against fellow students or administrative wardens without
substantiating evidence are strictly prohibited.
*(End of Official Residential Life & Hostel Administration Handbook)*
